passage: Zeenat, you know how I bit your head off yesterday about the project? I've figured something out. I've shot up this year; every pair of trousers is short, and I'm hungry all the time. When dinner's late at home, I turn into a different person. Last Sunday Papa asked about my marks before we'd eaten, and I shouted that he never lets me breathe. Then I had a big plate of rajma chawal and felt human again, and embarrassed. It's the same pattern every time: empty stomach, short fuse, blaming whoever's closest. So I've started saying, "Give me a bit, I have to eat first, then we can talk." Papa actually laughed and said, "Fine, Lokesh, food first." And I keep peanuts in my bag now. So, sorry about yesterday. I was starving, and you got the worst of me.

qa.a: Peanuts.

qa.a: Lokesh felt human again but also embarrassed about shouting at Papa.

qa.a: Zeenat may feel relieved to get an apology and an explanation, and less hurt about being snapped at over the project.

passage: I'm Sarika, Ankita's older sister, and this year I've watched her grow out of every pair of jeans she owns. At our cousin's wedding in Jaipur, lunch kept getting pushed back for the rituals. By afternoon Ankita had rolled her eyes at Bua, told me my dupatta looked "tragic" and was sitting alone on the steps, chin on her knees. I couldn't tell if she was sad about something bigger. Then she stood up and said, quite calmly, "Sarika di, I'm not angry with anyone. I just need food before I talk to people." We found the snacks counter, and she ate a plate of samosas. Soon she was dancing with the little cousins, and she went back to say sorry to Bua.

qa.q: What did Ankita say about Sarika's dupatta?
qa.a: That it looked "tragic".

qa.q: What does Ankita's calm line suggest she was feeling?
qa.a: She felt low and cranky from hunger, but was aware that it was not really anger at anyone.

qa.q: Which choice turned the afternoon around, and why?
qa.a: Ankita saying she needed food before talking and then eating; it met her body's need instead of letting the grumpiness land on relatives.

qa.q: How does Sarika see Ankita's moodiness at first?
qa.a: Sarika cannot tell whether it is sadness about something bigger, and only understands once Ankita names the hunger.

grounding: Illustrates a growing teenager getting sharp and low when a meal is delayed, then recognising it and asking to eat before talking.

subtype: Teen growth spurt appetite and grumpiness [Actor]
passage: Last year I grew nine centimetres in about eight months, and my stomach seemed to be running a separate business. I'm Kamal, and my sister Maria would tell you I was a monster at five o'clock. I'd come home from football, she'd ask a harmless question about the TV remote, and I'd bite her head off. Once I slammed my door so hard the mirror rattled. Then Mummy noticed something: I was sweet again twenty minutes after eating. So we tested it. On football days I carried a sandwich and ate it on the bus. And when I walked in still cranky, I started saying, "Food first, then talking." Maria rolled her eyes at that line at first. Now she hands me a banana at the door and says, "Talk later, monster."

qa.q: What did Kamal carry on football days?
qa.a: A sandwich, eaten on the bus.

qa.q: How did Kamal feel at five o'clock on football days?
qa.a: Kamal felt cranky and sharp, ready to snap at any harmless question because the growing body was demanding food.

qa.q: Why is "Food first, then talking" a useful line?
qa.a: It names the real cause and pauses the conversation, so Kamal does not take the hunger out on Maria.

qa.q: How does Maria's view of the five o'clock moods change?
qa.a: She moves from rolling her eyes to handing Kamal a banana at the door, seeing hunger rather than bad temper.

grounding: Shows a growing teenager turning sharp when meals are late, spotting the pattern, and learning to say they need to eat before talking.

passage:
Coach's note, swimming squad, Tuesday
Rajni was sharp with everyone at evening practice: she sulked through the warm-up, told Pooja to "get lost" in the lane, and cried when I corrected her stroke. This is the third evening like this. She has grown fast this year, and she trains straight after school, often without eating since lunch. After practice I sat with her on the stands and asked if she was hungry. She laughed, then said, "Starving, all the time." I suggested she pack a proper snack for the bus, and that when she feels the storm coming, she tell us, "I need to eat first." I rang her father this evening, and he is sending a tiffin with her from tomorrow.
Gurpreet

qa.q: What did Rajni tell Pooja in the lane?
qa.a: To "get lost".

qa.q: What was Rajni feeling during evening practice?
qa.a: She was irritable and low, close to tears, because she was starving after a growth spurt and a long gap since lunch.

qa.q: Why is Gurpreet's suggestion better than disciplining her for rudeness?
qa.a: It treats the mood as a body need, gives Rajni a plan to eat and words to say, and brings her father in so the tiffin comes daily.

qa.q: How might Pooja have felt after being told to get lost?
qa.a: Pooja was probably hurt and confused, not knowing Rajni was simply starving.

grounding: Shows a growing teenager turning sharp and low when food is late, and learning to say she needs to eat first instead of blaming others.

subtype: Teen growth spurt appetite and grumpiness [Actor]
passage:
Monday
Almost wrecked everything with Chandrika today. We were planning the science fair model after school, and she said my design was "a bit messy", and I just exploded. Called her a know-it-all. She walked off. I sat on the steps, stomach growling so loudly the watchman looked over, and realised I hadn't eaten since the 10 am break. It's been happening a lot. Mumma says I eat like a wrestler these days, and when dinner is late I'm horrible to everyone.
So, a new rule: when I feel that hot, snappy thing coming, I say, "Wait, I need to eat first." Messaged Chandrika at seven, after dal-chawal: "Sorry. I was starving and awful. Your point about the wiring is right." She sent a thumbs up. Tomorrow I'm packing two tiffins.
Gargi

qa.q: Since when had Gargi not eaten?
qa.a: Since the 10 am break.

qa.q: What was Gargi feeling while sitting on the steps?
qa.a: Gargi felt regretful and embarrassed after exploding, and very hungry, with a stomach growling loudly.

qa.q: What is wise about Gargi's new rule?
qa.a: Saying "Wait, I need to eat first" pauses a fight caused by hunger, so Gargi does not blame others for a body need.

qa.q: How might Chandrika have felt when called a know-it-all?
qa.a: Chandrika was likely hurt and annoyed, which is why she walked off, though the apology later seems to help.

grounding: Shows a growing teenager snapping at a friend after a long gap without food, spotting the pattern, and choosing to say they need to eat first.
